review_scope.snapshot: main at commit 7da237b (latest commit shown during review; dated Sep 25, 2026)
review_scope.review_method: Reviewed the repository landing page/tree, README, architecture and ops docs, prediction-engine/fantasy code and free-first ingestion code; then independently verified 100 candidate source pages from primary documentation or provider sites.
review_scope.counting_note: The 100 recommendations are distinct verified source pages/URLs. They represent 81 distinct domains; repeated vendors are intentional when separate products/pages expose materially different signal families. No recommendation should be treated as production-approved until rights, access, point-in-time behavior and redistribution terms are checked.

repository_understanding.product_position: A Next.js sports picks platform with PostgreSQL/Prisma, API routes, subscription/paywall surfaces, deterministic prediction/scoring code, ingestion adapters, workers and an operator cockpit; the README explicitly says it is in internal calibration only with no auto-publish, auto-send, external posting or automated betting.
repository_understanding.architecture_summary: The documented architecture has client, API, prediction, subscription, PostgreSQL data, ingestion and worker layers; the baseline flow is odds ingestion → normalization/freshness validation → database → pick generation → gated display/content.
repository_understanding.current_primary_ingestion: The documented primary provider is The Odds API for bookmaker h2h, spreads and totals; the repo also contains a free-first router with adapters/registrations for ESPN public scores, Open-Meteo, NCAA, Polymarket, Kalshi, MLB Stats API, NHL API, balldontlie, ESPN box scores and nflverse.
repository_understanding.free_first_and_rights_gate: Free-first ingestion is designed to choose a cleared free adapter, return provenance and only justify paid calls when no cleared free source covers the need; the code performs clearance checks before the ESPN score and Open-Meteo paths.
repository_understanding.prediction_engine: The prediction-engine package is described as a large TypeScript probabilistic forecasting/calibration/betting-intelligence library, but the signal-architecture review says many modules are orphaned, shadow, diagnostic or scripts-only rather than part of the certified publish path.
repository_understanding.fantasy_surface: The DFS optimizer supports cash, GPP and leverage modes, salary-cap lineups, locks/excludes, stacking and an exact search seeded by a heuristic; however the shipped DFS slate explicitly calls itself illustrative and uses fictional players/illustrative values.
repository_understanding.calibration_truth: The current-state document reports an eligibility sample around 339, Brier 0.2478 (RED against a ≤0.22 floor), ECE 0.0357 (GREEN), Murphy resolution thin, and no PROVEN claim; it says calibration adjustments and auto-publish remain off.

verified_strengths.finding: Clear operational safety posture: internal calibration, no auto-publish/auto-bet, and feature gates/empty states are explicit.
Rights-aware ingestion and free-first spend control are implemented as runtime concepts, not only prose.
The engine has substantial calibration, selective-publish, edge, settlement and audit concepts, and the signal architecture explicitly separates model probability from downstream withholding/display.
The DFS optimizer is glass-box and testable, with seeded deterministic heuristic search plus exact branch-and-bound and an independent oracle noted in the code.
The source graph treats clearance, freshness, conflicts, proof and source status as first-class concerns, and the gap audit records a large seeded candidate universe.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: Fantasy projections are not model-owned: the fantasy blocker says proj/ceiling/own values in dfs-slate.ts are manually authored constants and there is no training pipeline or pick-result feedback loop.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Replace illustrative constants with versioned, point-in-time projections trained from historical box scores, lines, roles, injuries and contest context; persist model version and feature snapshot.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: ADP is single-source and lazily refreshed; the blocker calls for a second ADP provider, freshness cron and discrepancy detection.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Ingest at least two rights-cleared ADP sources on a schedule, store as-of timestamps and alert on divergence before ranking.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: Rankings adapter exists but the blocker reports no live consumer in the pick-ranking pipeline.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Wire rankings into a named feature/gate with an explicit model-version proposal and walk-forward evaluation.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: The source-intelligence gap audit says active legally usable coverage is smaller than the seeded source universe and specifically calls out licensed route/pressure/coverage/tracking/PFF-like/trenches data.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Prioritize contracts/first-party feeds for tracking, charting, pressure, coverage, route and trench signals; keep candidate sources separate from active sources.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: The signal architecture reports that many research/engine modules are orphaned or scripts-only and that the edge-lab harness has not run on a schedule or in CI.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Create a source-to-feature-to-model registry with importer, owner, rights, freshness SLA, as-of semantics, test, backtest and kill condition; schedule the walk-forward/evaluation harness.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: The current calibration state is not publish-ready: Brier is red, the green streak is zero, and auto-publish/calibration adjustments remain off.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Do not expand public claims; accumulate settled, point-in-time rows, grade against close/settlement, and require pre-registered calibration and promotion gates.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: The architecture says odds freshness is central, but the signal audit reports no monitor for odds_line_snapshots and describes prior archive outages going unnoticed.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Add freshness/coverage monitors for every critical table and alert when source, book, sport or market coverage silently collapses.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: Health/recovery and sensitive player data are not equivalent to public injury news; they require consent, minimization, access controls and explicit rights.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Start with official public availability/status feeds; only add wearable/team-health integrations through consented contracts and a separate sensitive-data plane.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: The real-vs-stubbed audit says backtesting proof is fixture-backed rather than historical prediction proof and vendor adapters remain gated until keys/contracts exist.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Build a sealed historical prediction store with opening/as-of/closing lines, feature snapshots, labels, and reproducible walk-forward reports before claiming superiority.

highest_impact_gaps.gap: The repo’s own signal architecture says it has a measurement shortage, not merely a signal shortage: a large corpus exists but only a narrow set is proven to calibrate.
highest_impact_gaps.recommended_action: Invest in measurement infrastructure first: PIT snapshots, lineage, leakage tests, baseline comparisons, uncertainty intervals, calibration, CLV and subgroup drift.

source_selection_and_validation_rules.rule: Treat every recommendation below as a candidate source, not an automatic integration.
Require written rights/terms for commercial feeds, tracking, video, league pages and editorial content; do not infer scraping or redistribution permission from public visibility.
Store fetched_at, source_as_of, license/contract, parser version, raw hash and transformed feature version for every record.
Do not put a signal into a published probability until it survives point-in-time leakage tests, purged walk-forward evaluation, market-baseline comparison and a pre-registered kill line.
Use health, wearable, cognitive and biometric data only when athlete/team consent and legal basis exist; keep it isolated from public editorial feeds.
Prefer abstention/withholding when freshness, coverage, identity resolution, rights or calibration floors fail.

recommended_sources.name: MLB Baseball Savant Statcast CSV Documentation

recommended_sources.name: nflfastR
recommended_sources.category: football research dataset and modeling toolkit
recommended_sources.why_it_matters: The official package site documents NFL play-by-play back to 1999, expected-points/win-probability/completion-probability models, and nightly-updated complete-season datasets.

recommended_sources.name: Kaggle Sports Datasets

recommended_sources.name: TrueSkill Python Documentation
recommended_sources.why_it_matters: The documentation provides Bayesian rating objects for teams and players, match-quality/draw-probability calculations and an explicit two-team win-probability example, directly supporting sports outcome modeling.
recommended_sources.access_or_rights_note: The page documents installation via pip and an implementation API, but the fetched documentation does not state a separate data license; review the package's own license before redistribution.

recommended_sources.name: TrueSkill: A Bayesian Skill Rating System
recommended_sources.why_it_matters: The paper formalizes TrueSkill as a Bayesian factor-graph rating system that infers marginal skill distributions and models team outcomes, supplying a principled research basis for probability forecasts.
recommended_sources.access_or_rights_note: The citation is a research-paper PDF, not a data feed or API; use of the publication and any derived implementation should follow the publisher/Microsoft copyright and licensing conditions.

recommended_sources.name: scikit-learn Probability Calibration

recommended_sources.name: tidymodels Model Calibration

recommended_sources.access_or_rights_note: The page is educational documentation and does not provide sports data or a separate commercial data license; software and package use remain subject to their respective licenses.

recommended_sources.name: NannyML Probability Calibration

recommended_sources.access_or_rights_note: This citation is a technical article rather than a sports dataset or API; it does not grant rights to any third-party examples, and product/package licensing should be checked separately.

source_list_notes: Priority is an engineering prioritization for closing the gaps documented in this repository, not a claim that any provider is approved or superior.
The list includes commercial feeds, public official pages, research datasets and software/evaluation documentation. Their access and legal status differ; each item carries a conservative rights note.

Several entries are separate products/pages from the same vendor. The list contains 100 verified source URLs and 81 distinct domains; deduplicate at procurement/integration time where one contract can cover multiple products.

The strongest immediate path is not ingesting all 100. Start with the high-priority rows that address fantasy projections, injuries/availability, schedules/rosters, odds/market depth, weather/travel and evaluation baselines; shadow the rest.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: The durable schema is still fundamentally a betting-pick system, not a model-owned fantasy system: Pick supports only SPREAD/TOTAL/MONEYLINE-style selections and a single active pick per game/pickType, while the schema has no contest, lineup, roster slot, salary, projection distribution, ownership, or player-projection artifact model.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Add first-class Contest, ContestSlate, PlayerProjection, ProjectionDistribution, PlayerEligibility, Lineup, LineupSlot, SalarySnapshot, OwnershipProjection, and OptimizationRun entities. Version each artifact and preserve the exact inputs, scoring rules, and constraints used to generate a lineup; do not overload Pick or JSON blobs.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review emphasized prediction/fantasy code and UI surfaces; the schema shows that the durable source of truth remains game-market picks, so apparent fantasy breadth is not backed by a corresponding persistence model.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: Player identity is materially NFL/nflverse-specific even though a generic Entity/EntityEdge graph exists: Player requires a unique gsisId, and PlayerGameStat uses NFL season/week fields; SnapCount, Injury, and DepthChartEntry retain nullable/unresolved player IDs and free-text names. This creates silent cross-source fragmentation and makes multi-sport fantasy identity unsafe.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Make canonical identity sport-scoped and provider-neutral. Add provider identifier rows with uniqueness by provider/sport/id, explicit resolution decisions and confidence, alias history, effective dates, and rejection/quarantine states. Require projection and stat facts to reference a resolved canonical entity or an auditable unresolved record.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The generic entity graph looks like an identity solution at a glance, but the operational fantasy tables still use NFL-specific identifiers and nullable links; reviewing only the graph or ingestion adapters would overvalue completeness.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: Model governance is represented as free-text modelVersion fields rather than a durable model registry: Pick, ShadowSignal, PerformanceSummary, CalibrationProposal, and LadderEvent carry strings, but there is no schema-level model artifact, feature-set hash, training-data snapshot, code commit, approval, or promotion relation tying a prediction to an immutable model package.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Create ModelArtifact/ModelVersion and ModelPromotion tables with immutable artifact URI/hash, source commit, feature and label schema hashes, training window, calibration version, owner, approval decision, status, and rollback lineage. Replace free-text modelVersion with a foreign key or immutable registry key and require prediction writes to resolve it.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The repository has extensive calibration and shadow-engine vocabulary, which can be mistaken for model ownership; the database contract reveals that provenance is largely a string convention.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: The pure backtest harness has a real anti-leakage strength: it removes homeScore and awayScore before invoking the scorer, rejects empty/malformed corpora, and separates pushes from decided win rate. However, its report aggregates wins/losses/pushes and decided win rate only; it does not itself enforce time-ordered train/test splits, player-level leakage boundaries, ROI/utility, calibration, ranking, or fantasy objective metrics.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Keep the leakage guard, then make evaluation a versioned protocol: temporal train/validation/holdout partitions, as-of feature timestamps, entity/season leakage checks, Brier/log loss/calibration and fantasy ranking/utility metrics, bankroll/contest simulation, confidence intervals, and a machine-readable evaluation receipt required for promotion.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Prior work likely credited the existence of a backtest harness as equivalent to a complete evaluation system; the fetched implementation is deliberately narrow and market-pick oriented.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: The source registry is a genuine hidden strength: it encodes license, commercial-use, attribution, robots, rate limit, verdict, datasets, and an assertIngestible guard. But it explicitly allows use-with-caution sources into the ingestible verdict set even though its own comment defines that class as having no written commercial grant; that is not a safe default for a model-owned commercial feature store.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Split technical ingestion from product eligibility. Permit caution sources only into quarantined research storage, never into training, customer-facing projections, or derived features unless an explicit owner/legal decision and rights snapshot is attached. Enforce that policy at dataset promotion and feature materialization, not only at fetch time.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior source-page review likely emphasized breadth and the presence of legal controls; the important contradiction is in the registry's own verdict semantics and admission set.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: Observability is optional and intentionally incomplete: Sentry becomes a no-op when DSNs are absent, and the integration omits source-map upload. A production deployment can therefore report an apparently clean runtime while dropping exception telemetry and providing minified stack frames, which is inadequate for an autonomous model/pipeline owner.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Make production observability a deployment gate: require DSN and release identifiers, upload source maps, attach model/version/data-source/run IDs to traces, and persist durable worker run outcomes and alert delivery failures independently of Sentry. Keep no-op behavior for local development only.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Observability is easy to over-credit from the presence of a Sentry wrapper; the fetched implementation explicitly documents no-op operation and no source maps.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: The data-refresh worker documents a fail-open path when the paid-odds governor cannot be constructed. That preserves availability but can allow paid requests without a functioning credit governor, undermining spend caps and making model-input reproducibility dependent on an external paid feed's mutable state.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Fail closed for production paid ingestion when the ledger/governor cannot be constructed; use an explicit owner-approved emergency mode with a hard request ceiling, durable reason, and alert. Persist the exact odds snapshot and governor decision alongside every model-input build.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The worker's pacing, quota cutoff, and ledger terminology read as safety controls, but the construction-failure policy reverses the required default for a model-owned paid-data plane.

second_pass_findings.area: Current repository deep audit: data model, model ownership, evaluation, identity, rights, workers, auth and observability for a model-owned fantasy/prediction system
second_pass_findings.finding: Authentication and administrative ownership include a hard-coded owner allowlist in application source. The code documents that these addresses are always-admin and can reach cockpit surfaces independently of ADMIN_EMAILS, creating a deployment-coupled authority path that is difficult to rotate, audit, or revoke through normal data governance.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Move ownership and model-promotion authority to a database-backed, audited role/grant system with key rotation and explicit scopes (read, publish, promote, kill switch). Keep bootstrap access time-limited and require a break-glass receipt for production use.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review likely focused on authentication correctness and paywall behavior; it did not treat hard-coded operational authority as a model-governance risk.

second_pass_findings.area: Missing and underleveraged model/evaluation infrastructure for fantasy and sports prediction
second_pass_findings.finding: The repository has a credible time-ordered calibration path: its calibration runbook specifies a time hold-out, fitting only on the hold-out/training side, reliability/ECE/Brier outputs, and a selected (+EV) slice. That is stronger than a generic random split, but it is not yet a complete point-in-time feature contract: the runbook does not document feature availability/created timestamps, correction/backfill handling, or an as-of join test. Feast explicitly warns that event-time-only joins can return values backfilled after the entity timestamp, and offers created-timestamp filtering to prevent that leakage (https://docs.feast.dev/getting-started/concepts/point-in-time-joins).
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Make every feature carry event_time and available_at/created_at; build training snapshots by decision timestamp; add a test that a post-cutoff correction, late injury report, or closing line cannot enter a pre-kickoff row. Version the snapshot and source timestamps with each prediction.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: A review centered on ingestion and candidate source pages can see data breadth without testing whether the value was knowable at lineup-lock or kickoff; the repository runbook exposes the split but not a full feature-store availability contract (https://github.com/Beexly/Sports/blob/main/docs/ops/CALIBRATION_PIPELINE.md).

second_pass_findings.area: Missing and underleveraged model/evaluation infrastructure for fantasy and sports prediction
second_pass_findings.finding: Calibration is materially underleveraged as a decision/evaluation layer. The repo documents ECE and Brier/reliability reporting and recently added an honest probability resolver that excludes spread/total rank scores from probability scoring (https://github.com/Beexly/Sports/blob/main/docs/ops/CALIBRATION_PIPELINE.md; https://github.com/Beexly/Sports/commit/2c27590a1a26d7dca6b301ead16a88eaeff1087e). A sports-betting study found calibration-driven model selection materially outperformed accuracy-driven selection in its NBA experiment, reporting average ROI +34.69% versus -35.17% (https://arxiv.org/html/2303.06021v4).
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Promote proper scoring and decision evaluation to model-selection gates: log loss/Brier for categorical outcomes; CRPS or interval score for player fantasy points; calibration by sport, market, horizon, probability bin, and odds/ownership bucket; then evaluate expected utility under contest payout, entry fee, limits, and fractional-Kelly risk rather than accuracy alone.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Prediction reviews commonly emphasize hit rate and model presence; the repo's own calibration material is operationally framed as an offline/R&D path rather than an always-on model registry gate (https://github.com/Beexly/Sports/blob/main/docs/ops/CALIBRATION_PIPELINE.md).

second_pass_findings.area: Missing and underleveraged model/evaluation infrastructure for fantasy and sports prediction
second_pass_findings.finding: Uncertainty infrastructure exists but is easy to overread: the repository's Jackknife+ addition explicitly reports a 1-2a coverage floor, refuses unreachable order statistics, and does not claim the usual 1-a guarantee (https://github.com/Beexly/Sports/commit/7b2506a9b6ae38e321df94739c9981e135fb25e8). Conformal prediction provides finite-sample, distribution-free set/interval guarantees under its assumptions and can wrap any pre-trained model (https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511).
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Attach coverage, width, abstention/refusal, and conditional-coverage diagnostics to every sport/position/horizon; use rolling, non-exchangeable/time-series conformal variants for sequential games; block production promotion when coverage collapses or intervals become implausibly wide.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The feature is recent and deliberately additive/dark (the commit says no gate was flipped), so a prior code review could count the implementation without assessing whether uncertainty reaches lineup decisions (https://github.com/Beexly/Sports/commit/7b2506a9b6ae38e321df94739c9981e135fb25e8).

second_pass_findings.area: Missing and underleveraged model/evaluation infrastructure for fantasy and sports prediction
second_pass_findings.finding: The pipeline does not document coherent hierarchical probabilistic forecasts for the fantasy hierarchy (player minutes/stat lines to team totals, slate totals, and contest outcomes). Forecast reconciliation literature shows independently produced base forecasts can violate aggregation constraints and describes MinT reconciliation to minimize total forecast-error variance (https://otexts.com/fpp3/reconciliation.html).
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Model player-level distributions jointly with team/game latent variables; reconcile minutes, possessions, team totals, and player stat sums; score both bottom-level fantasy points and aggregate coherence. Preserve covariance so lineup simulations do not independently overstate tails.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: A source/ingestion review tends to assess whether player and team feeds exist, not whether downstream forecasts sum consistently or preserve cross-player covariance.

second_pass_findings.area: Missing and underleveraged model/evaluation infrastructure for fantasy and sports prediction
second_pass_findings.finding: Ranking and ownership are not represented as a complete probabilistic contest model in the fetched calibration documentation. The repository's ranking-basis census only measures which fallback key (including confidence/100) drives sorting (https://github.com/Beexly/Sports/commit/7b2506a9b6ae38e321df94739c9981e135fb25e8), while fantasy decisions require joint simulations of score, selection/ownership, correlation, payout structure, and field duplication.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Separate predictive probability from ranking score; estimate ownership/selection probabilities with time-sliced calibration; simulate correlated player outcomes and opponent lineups; report expected value, top-percentile finish probability, downside, and duplication-adjusted utility by contest type.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review covered prediction/fantasy code, but a ranking-key census can look like ranking infrastructure while still not measuring ownership uncertainty or contest-level decision utility.

second_pass_findings.area: Missing and underleveraged model/evaluation infrastructure for fantasy and sports prediction
second_pass_findings.finding: Drift monitoring is a missing production-model layer. Evidently distinguishes feature/data drift, concept drift, prediction drift, training-serving skew, and data quality, and recommends statistical tests, distance metrics, and rule checks; it also notes drift is only a proxy when labels are delayed (https://www.evidentlyai.com/ml-in-production/data-drift).
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Monitor feature, odds, injury-status, line-movement, prediction, calibration, and settlement-lag drift by league and season phase; maintain delayed-label performance dashboards; trigger recalibration/retraining or abstention on predeclared thresholds, with a champion/challenger history.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Ingestion freshness and source coverage are not the same as distributional or concept-drift monitoring; the distinction is easy to miss when the review is organized around feeds.

second_pass_findings.area: Missing and underleveraged model/evaluation infrastructure for fantasy and sports prediction
second_pass_findings.finding: The sports study identifies injuries and in-game events as influential context that many predictive models omit, and notes that streaming events require a different processing path (https://arxiv.org/html/2303.06021v4). The fetched repository materials show calibration and shadow evaluation, but do not establish a causal injury/news uncertainty model or a principled stale-information fallback.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Represent injury status as an event-time distribution (availability probability, minutes restriction, replacement effects), separate observed from inferred reports, run scenario simulations for late scratches, and abstain or widen uncertainty when status freshness/identity confidence is below threshold.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The previous ingestion review could verify injury/news sources, but source existence does not prove causal propagation into minutes, usage, teammates, opponent effects, or uncertainty.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: The largest underleveraged signal family is optical/player tracking rather than box-score data: NBA Stats explicitly exposes player speed/distance tracking, identifies Second Spectrum as the provider, and warns that tracking is not available for every game. That is both high predictive value and a material missingness problem.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Add a tracking adapter with availability flags, provider/version metadata, and sport-specific features (distance, speed, spacing, workload); never impute unavailable games as zero.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: A conventional review of prediction/fantasy code can value player statistics without distinguishing event totals from sensor-derived movement data and its coverage gaps.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: MLB Statcast is a concrete public signal surface spanning bat tracking, pitch/location, pop time, catch probability, jump, and sprint speed, not just standard statistics.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize Statcast feature ingestion for contact quality, baserunning, defense and pitcher/batter matchup models, retaining leaderboard filters and season snapshots.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior scope emphasized repository code and candidate source pages; an interactive official leaderboard is easy to treat as a presentation page rather than a machine-readable signal catalog.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Hudl StatsBomb documents unusually granular football event data (over 3,400 events per match) plus player-location data for 40-plus leagues and freeze-frame inputs such as goalkeeper/defender locations.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Add an event/tactical schema capable of freeze frames, pressure, locations and possession context; use it for xG, buildup, recruitment and tactical-state features rather than only goals/shots.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Generic match feeds obscure the difference between event-level tactical context and aggregate match statistics.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Hudl Wyscout supplies a complementary video-plus-data scouting corpus from more than 1,000 competitions, making video retrieval, clip labels and player evaluation a distinct signal family.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Treat video as a licensed feature store: persist clip IDs/time ranges and derived labels, not copied media, and join clips to stable player/match IDs.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review covered prediction and ingestion, but likely valued structured feeds more than multimodal evidence and its rights constraints.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Genius Sports advertises official, low-latency live and historical data and explicitly includes play-by-play for broadcasters plus betting/fantasy use cases; it states it is official NFL/NCAA partner and serves 400-plus leagues.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Evaluate as a licensed event-by-event backbone for competitions where rights and latency matter; record competition entitlement and redistribution restrictions per contract.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: A long source list can include data vendors without separating official league partnerships, latency, and commercial licensing from free/public accessibility.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Sportradar's documented offering covers 80-plus sports, 500-plus leagues and 750,000-plus events annually, with historical data and XML/JSON delivery; its developer portal exposes separate APIs for football, basketball, hockey, baseball and racing.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Use it as an enterprise breadth/normalization benchmark and test only under a trial or commercial agreement; do not assume public API availability.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Provider breadth can be undervalued when a repository prototype is judged mainly on free endpoints rather than coverage, reliability and rights.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Stats Perform's STATS API documents live game statistics, editorial coverage, photos, situational player/team statistics, historical data and common IDs, but requires an access key.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Use common IDs as a cross-provider identity bridge and separate editorial/photo entitlements from numerical-stat entitlements in ingestion configuration.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Identity resolution and media/editorial products are often collapsed into the numeric feed discussion.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Opta (Stats Perform) explicitly markets live data, AI tools, advanced content, ultrafast data, dynamic stats APIs, betting data and sports-news video, supporting a layered event-plus-media architecture.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Model event, trading, video and derived-insight products as separate licensed products; request sport/competition-level sample payloads before committing to a common schema.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: A source may be counted once even though its event, betting, video and insight products have different access and rights.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: KINEXON describes real-time player and ball tracking, advanced performance analytics, millisecond-accurate officiating, athlete health/availability and a biomechanics partnership, making it relevant to load, injury and officiating signals unavailable in public box scores.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Keep as a team/league partnership lead rather than assume an open feed; design consent, privacy, sensor calibration and aggregation controls before using athlete-level data.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Commercial performance technology is not normally exposed through public sports APIs and can be missed by URL-based source reviews.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: FlightAware AeroAPI provides queryable current and historical flight data, including ETA, last position, full track, ground speed and altitude, with history back to 2011.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Build a travel/rest feature pipeline from team itineraries only where legally and operationally available; cache flight tracks and derive time-zone crossings, delays and turnaround time.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Travel is external to the game-stat schema and is usually absent from fantasy-oriented repositories, despite plausible rest and fatigue effects.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: The U.S. National Weather Service API is a primary forecast/observation source and its documentation links forecast, aviation, marine, climate and past-weather services; this supports venue-time weather joins rather than generic city weather.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Join hourly forecast and observed conditions to venue coordinates and scheduled start time, preserving issue time, forecast horizon and units; include wind, precipitation, temperature and visibility.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Weather is frequently treated as a one-off scrape or narrative note instead of a versioned forecast-vs-observation feature with leakage controls.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: OpenStreetMap offers open map data usable for venue geocoding and facility context, but requires attribution and follows open-data licensing conditions.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Use OSM for venue coordinates, travel distance and surrounding elevation/urban context where suitable; store attribution and validate stadium surface/roof details from venue or league sources.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Facilities and surface are not represented by typical score APIs, while map data is often overlooked as a feature source.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: SportsDataIO documents a developer catalog with competition coverage and available feeds across NFL, MLB, NBA and NHL, and advertises free exploration alongside commercial feeds; it is a practical bridge for injuries, lineups, depth charts and fantasy-oriented feeds, but entitlement must be checked per feed.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Inventory feed-level availability (injury, lineup, depth chart, salary/DFS, play-by-play) and enforce key/rate/redistribution limits in configuration rather than hard-coding assumptions.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior 100-source pass may have counted a provider name without checking its separate feed catalog and commercial/free split.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Sportradar's developer documentation exposes league-specific endpoint families and a 30-day marketplace trial, but this is not evidence of production redistribution rights.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Add a rights ledger: trial, internal research, production display, betting/fantasy, historical retention and redistribution should be separate states.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Technical documentation is easy to mistake for permission to use or republish the feed.

second_pass_findings.area: Sports signal expansion: tracking, event, tactical/video, travel, weather, facilities, identity, and fantasy/rights-aware providers
second_pass_findings.finding: Hawk-Eye's tennis page did not expose substantive content in the fetched result, so it should be treated as a lead requiring direct commercial verification rather than claimed availability of ball-tracking or officiating data.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Do not build against it from marketing-page assumptions; obtain an API/sample contract and verify sport, tour, historical access and redistribution rights.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Sparse or JS-heavy provider pages can create false confidence when a source list records the brand but not verified access.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The repository has extensive launch and feature gates, but the inspected production contract does not establish service-level objectives, error budgets, on-call ownership, restore objectives, or a tested disaster-recovery procedure. The runbook is primarily a manual staging/route checklist, while OpenTelemetry defines SLI/SLO concepts that are absent from that runbook.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Add a versioned reliability contract: availability/latency/freshness/settlement SLIs, SLOs and error budgets; page thresholds; owner/escalation; RTO/RPO; backup-restore evidence; and a scheduled failover/restore exercise. Instrument API, ingestion, workers, Stripe webhooks, and settlement with metrics, structured logs, and traces.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review covered architecture and ingestion, but a launch checklist can look operationally complete without defining measurable reliability targets or proving recovery.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The env contract contains OAuth client secrets, NextAuth secret, Stripe secrets/webhook secret, odds-provider key, Anthropic key, and Redis/database connection settings, but the inspected materials do not provide a production secret-rotation schedule, least-privilege matrix, KMS/secret-manager requirement, or incident revocation playbook. CI's secret scan and dependency audit are useful gates, not runtime credential controls.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Move production secrets to a managed secret store; document per-service scopes, rotation/expiry, break-glass access, webhook replay protection, and revoke/rotate steps. Add automated secret-age/permission checks and ensure logs redact tokens, OAuth artifacts, payment identifiers, and user identifiers.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review examined code and ingestion behavior, whereas the deployment-risk boundary is concentrated in the environment contract and operational controls.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The Prisma schema stores OAuth access_token, refresh_token, and id_token fields as text, and also stores user email/name/image plus billing identifiers. The repository README describes Google sign-in and Stripe but the inspected repo materials do not show a privacy notice, records of processing, subject-access/erasure/export workflow, consent ledger, retention/deletion policy for account data, or processor/subprocessor register.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Minimize OAuth persistence (prefer provider-managed sessions where possible), encrypt sensitive fields, isolate billing/security evidence, and implement authenticated export, correction, deletion/restriction, consent withdrawal, retention jobs, and an auditable lawful-basis/purpose/subprocessor inventory. Publish a privacy notice before public launch.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Prior coverage emphasized product/data pipelines, not the personal-data inventory revealed by the schema.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The README explicitly says the promotions surface is compliance-gated and the env file discusses terms consent, but the inspected launch materials do not establish jurisdictional age/location checks, responsible-gambling self-exclusion or harm signals, marketing consent/withdrawal, or a documented boundary between an affiliate promotion and regulated gambling activity. The Gambling Commission says gambling operators must continue processing data needed for licensing and social-responsibility objectives, and that regulatory-compliance data may need at least five years after the customer relationship ends.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Before enabling promotions/fantasy/betting-adjacent flows, obtain jurisdiction-specific legal sign-off; implement age/geo gates, licensed-operator and offer eligibility checks, prominent affiliate/ad disclosures and terms, responsible-gambling links, self-exclusion suppression, consent/preference records, complaint handling, and a retention schedule that distinguishes regulatory evidence from marketing analytics.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review valued the visible compliance verdict/publish gates; it did not test whether those gates cover the operator-level safeguarding and retention obligations that arise once money, promotions, or gambling referrals are live.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The product presents a deterministic factor model and an accountability/calibration cockpit, but the inspected customer/launch documentation does not require a versioned, per-pick explanation containing factor contributions, input timestamps/source lineage, uncertainty/calibration, stale-data status, and correction/appeal path. NIST describes trustworthy AI as including validity/reliability, safety, security, accountability/transparency, explainability, privacy enhancement, and fairness.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Make an explanation artifact part of pick publication eligibility: model/data versions, factors and weights, missingness, market/line timestamp, confidence/calibration interval, limitations, and immutable audit linkage. Provide plain-language customer explanations and an operator correction/withdrawal workflow; test explanations against the actual score.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The earlier review recognized readable math and prediction code, but readability of implementation is not the same as a user-facing, reproducible explanation or fairness/safety evidence.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The CI workflow runs tests, migration checks, guardrails, secret scanning, and dependency auditing, but the fetched workflow does not document DAST/API authorization tests, abuse/rate-limit tests, container/IaC scanning, SBOM/provenance/signing, or a security incident response gate. OWASP specifically identifies broken object/function authorization, unrestricted resource consumption, sensitive business flows, SSRF, security misconfiguration, improper inventory, and unsafe API consumption as API risks relevant to admin, billing, ingestion, and trigger-refresh surfaces.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Add threat-model-backed tests for every admin/API route and tenant/object boundary; enforce rate limits and idempotency on refresh, checkout, webhook, export, and alert endpoints; add SAST/DAST, container/IaC and SBOM/provenance checks; and require a reviewed vulnerability disclosure and incident-response runbook before launch.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Static guardrails and unit tests are easy to count as 'security coverage'; the missed risk is runtime authorization, abuse economics, and dependency/infrastructure supply-chain assurance.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The repository has launch observatory pages and metric inventories, but the inspected materials do not define product-measurement semantics for activation, paid conversion, churn/refunds, affiliate disclosure exposure, responsible-gambling incidents, pick impressions-to-action, calibration by sport/market, or experiment guardrails. Without event schemas, denominators, versioning, and privacy limits, dashboards can create misleading success signals.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Create a measurement plan with event names/schema/owner, consent and minimization rules, stable denominators, cohort and sport/market slices, model/data-version dimensions, bot/duplicate handling, confidence intervals, and stop criteria for safety, complaints, refunds, stale data, and calibration regressions. Review it in the launch gate.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: Prior review focused on whether performance claims were gated, not whether the underlying product and safety metrics are defined well enough to support a launch decision.

second_pass_findings.area: Production reliability, privacy/consent, data rights, explainability, user safety, betting/fantasy compliance, security, monitoring, product measurement, and launch gates
second_pass_findings.finding: The repository's current-mode statement says internal calibration only, no auto-publish, no auto-send, no external posting, and no automated betting; that is a strong safety posture, but it is not itself a launch gate. The inspected docs do not show a single signed release checklist requiring privacy/age/geo review, security threat-model disposition, restore drill, observability readiness, explanation samples, payment/affiliate reconciliation, and rollback owner before public flags are enabled.
second_pass_findings.recommended_action: Turn the current safeguards into a fail-closed promotion gate with named approvers and evidence links: legal/privacy, safety/compliance, security, reliability, data-rights, model/explainability, payments, and support. Require canary exposure, rollback rehearsal, kill switches, and post-launch review before enabling each flag independently.
second_pass_findings.why_missed_before: The prior review likely credited the many flags and frozen modes as completed controls; the gap is governance evidence and launch accountability, not merely feature gating.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Underleveraged: calibration is treated mainly as an offline/reporting capability rather than the promotion criterion for model selection and product decisions.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: Make proper scoring, reliability, segment calibration and decision utility first-class model-registry gates; accuracy or hit rate alone is insufficient for probability-driven fantasy and market decisions.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Underleveraged: the repository has shadow signals, evidence, source freshness, ranking and proof vocabulary, but the durable schema still centers on market picks and free-text modelVersion values.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: Build fantasy projection, distribution, ownership, contest, lineup and model-artifact entities rather than hiding them in Pick or unversioned JSON.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Overvalued: a large backtest harness and many tests can look like historical proof, but the core harness removes outcomes and reports win/loss/push summaries without fantasy objectives, calibration, time-sliced training, contest utility or a promotion receipt.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: Retain the outcome-removal guard, then add a sealed point-in-time evaluation protocol and machine-readable evidence receipt before any superiority claim.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Underleveraged: the source registry and evidence graph are strong primitives, but use-with-caution data can still be technically ingestible.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: Separate technical ingestion from product/training eligibility; caution or unresolved-rights data belongs in quarantined research storage only.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Underleveraged: uncertainty code exists, but the repository explicitly avoids claiming a usual Jackknife+ guarantee and does not show that interval coverage reaches lineup decisions.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: Publish coverage, interval width and refusal rates by sport/position/horizon; use time-aware conformal methods and gate on coverage collapse or unusably wide intervals.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Underleveraged: player-tracking, event and tactical data are more valuable than simply adding more box-score feeds, but the second pass still found major commercial/contract boundaries.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: Prioritize one contracted tracking/event partner and one first-party/public advanced-stat lane per sport; do not try to recreate exclusive raw tracking without rights.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Overvalued: free-first coverage and many adapters do not imply reproducible, point-in-time training data.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: A source is production-useful only when identity, rights, as-of availability, correction history, freshness, conflict policy and retention are all captured.

underleveraged_or_overvalued.item: Underleveraged: current internal-calibration/no-auto-publish posture is a meaningful safety control, but not a release proof.
underleveraged_or_overvalued.implication: Convert it into a signed, fail-closed promotion gate covering legal/privacy, data rights, security, SLO/restore, explanation samples, payments and rollback ownership.

integration_sprint.objective: Move from an impressive, safety-gated market-pick platform with illustrative DFS surfaces to a real, model-owned fantasy/prediction data product whose projections are reproducible, calibrated, contest-aware, rights-cleared and explainable.
integration_sprint.ordering_principle: Do not add more signal breadth until identity, point-in-time availability, durable model artifacts and evaluation receipts are real; otherwise extra feeds increase apparent sophistication without increasing trustworthy accuracy.

sprints.sprint: S0 — Truth, identity and rights freeze
sprints.timebox_recommendation: First implementation sprint; complete before training a production fantasy model.
deliverables: Canonical sport-scoped entity IDs and provider-ID crosswalks with effective dates, aliases, resolution confidence and quarantine states.
Immutable raw SourceSnapshot plus source_as_of, fetched_at, available_at/created_at, correction lineage, parser version, raw hash, rights snapshot and license status.
Separate technical ingestion from cleared-for-training and cleared-for-customer publication states.
Fail-closed paid-data governor in production; explicit emergency mode with hard ceiling and audit receipt.
Production observability contract: source, worker, model, data-build and prediction-run IDs on logs/traces.
acceptance_tests: A post-event correction, late injury report or closing line cannot enter a pre-lock training row.
No unresolved or caution-rights record can materialize into a customer projection.
Any provider/governor/identity failure produces a visible blocked or stale state, never a silent fallback.

sprints.sprint: S1 — Durable fantasy slate and contest plane
sprints.timebox_recommendation: Second implementation sprint; start with one sport and one contest family.
deliverables: Contest, ContestSlate, ContestRule, SalarySnapshot, PlayerEligibility, RosterSlot, ProjectionRun, Lineup and LineupSlot entities.
Real contest/slate/salary/roster-slot ingestion with lock time, scoring rules, late-swap rules and source lineage.
Canonical player/team/game crosswalk and historical effective-dated roles/depth charts.
Replace fictional/illustrative DFS rows with a clearly blocked empty state until real inputs pass the rights and freshness gate.
acceptance_tests: A slate can be reconstructed exactly from persisted salary, eligibility, contest rules and lock-time snapshots.
A player cannot be selected if identity, sport, game, position, team or eligibility is unresolved.
Optimizer output references a durable ProjectionRun and ContestSlate, not hard-coded constants.

sprints.sprint: S2 — Point-in-time feature and label store
sprints.timebox_recommendation: Third implementation sprint; build once and reuse across all sports.
deliverables: FeatureDefinition registry with owner, sport, source, rights, event_time, available_at, transform version, missingness policy and kill condition.
Historical training-set builder that performs event-time plus created/available-time filtering.
Label ledger with outcome definition, settlement time, scoring-rule version and revision/void handling.
Feature snapshots keyed by decision timestamp and model/feature-set hash; no live table reads during training.
acceptance_tests: As-of replay at any historical lock time returns the same feature values and missingness state.
Leakage tests inject future values, backfills and outcomes and verify they are excluded.
Training and online serving share the same feature transformation contract.

sprints.timebox_recommendation: Fourth implementation sprint; productionize one sport/position family before broadening.
deliverables: A market-only/role-only baseline and a sport-specific hierarchical model with partial pooling across player, team, opponent, venue and season.
Separate availability/minutes/role model from per-minute production model; propagate uncertainty from availability and role into stat-line distributions.
Joint team/game latent variables so player outcomes preserve game totals, shared pace/possessions and teammate/opponent correlation.
Distributional outputs: median, quantiles, floor/ceiling, variance, probability over thresholds and scenario states—not only a point projection.
ModelArtifact/ModelVersion registry with artifact hash, code commit, feature schema hash, training window, label schema, calibration version, owner, approval and rollback lineage.
acceptance_tests: Every published projection resolves to one immutable model artifact and one feature snapshot.
Player and team forecasts are coherent under the chosen aggregation constraints.
Missing or uncertain role/injury inputs widen distributions or abstain rather than silently imputing certainty.

sprints.sprint: S4 — Calibration, uncertainty and sealed evaluation
sprints.timebox_recommendation: Fifth implementation sprint; no public superiority claim before this gate.
deliverables: Purged, time-ordered train/validation/holdout protocol with season/game/player grouping rules.
Proper scoring and calibration dashboard: log loss/Brier for probabilities, CRPS or interval score for distributions, reliability/ECE, calibration slope/intercept, sharpness and coverage.
Time-aware conformal or other uncertainty wrapper with coverage and interval-width diagnostics by sport, position, horizon, contest type and data-quality bucket.
Benchmark report against market-only, consensus, naive rolling and current deterministic baselines.
Machine-readable EvaluationReceipt that records dataset snapshot, model artifact, code commit, metrics, confidence intervals, slices, leakage checks and promotion decision.
acceptance_tests: Holdout rows are never used for fitting or calibration parameter selection.
Promotion requires pre-registered metric floors and no red subgroup failure; exact existing calibration floors remain the source of truth until ratified.
The current Brier-red/non-PROVEN state cannot be relabeled PROVEN by UI copy alone.

sprints.sprint: S5 — Ownership, correlation and contest decision engine
sprints.timebox_recommendation: Sixth implementation sprint; only after S1–S4 produce real distributions.
deliverables: Ownership/selection model with time-sliced training and calibration, separated from player performance probability.
Contest utility layer using payout structure, entry fee, roster constraints, field size and duplication risk.
Joint simulation of player outcomes, ownership and opponent-lineup construction; cash, GPP and leverage are separate decision policies.
Simulation-based optimizer that consumes distributions and covariance, not static proj/ceiling/ownership constants.
Post-lock result ledger linking lineup, forecast distribution, realized points, rank, payout, duplication and decision rationale.
acceptance_tests: Optimizer output is stable under seed replay and can be reproduced from the persisted run.
Contest objective changes output in a measurable way; cash and GPP are not only labels over one ranking.
Ownership uncertainty and correlation are visible in expected value, top-percentile probability and downside.

sprints.sprint: S6 — High-value signal activation in shadow mode
sprints.timebox_recommendation: Run incrementally after the baseline is stable; activate one factor at a time.
deliverables: Official injuries/transactions/lineups, weather/venue/travel, tactical/event data, officials and role/depth-chart signals with as-of logs.
One contracted tracking/event source per priority sport, plus lawful public substitutes such as Statcast/NBA tracking/StatsBomb open data where permitted.
Scenario engine for late scratches, minutes limits, weather changes, travel disruption and lineup changes.
Narrative/social/news signals captured with timestamps and reliability/bot/manipulation controls; shadow/withhold first, publish only after calibration evidence.
Sensitive health/wearable/cognitive data isolated behind consent, purpose limitation and access control.
acceptance_tests: Each factor has a source, owner, rights state, freshness SLA, sample-size threshold, backtest report and kill condition.
No new factor changes the public model until an isolated ablation and walk-forward result beats the baseline without harming calibration.
Stale or conflicting signals produce a reasoned scenario/abstention state.

sprints.sprint: S7 — Production reliability, safety and evidence UX
sprints.timebox_recommendation: Final pre-launch sprint; ship only as independently gated capability flags.
deliverables: Champion/challenger registry, drift dashboards, data-quality tests, source/worker/model SLOs, error budgets, alert ownership and restore/failover evidence.
Per-projection evidence artifact: source snapshots, timestamps, feature contributions, missingness, interval/coverage, calibration, model version, counter-evidence and correction path.
Production security gates for object/function authorization, abuse/rate-limit economics, SSRF, API inventory, secrets, SBOM and incident response.
Privacy, deletion/export/retention, consent and sensitive-data policies; age/geo/responsible-gaming/affiliate controls before money or promotions.
Public claims compiler that cannot say proven/accurate/superior unless the linked evaluation receipt and current gates pass.
acceptance_tests: A restore drill, rollback drill and kill-switch drill produce evidence owned by named operators.
A customer can understand what was known, when it was known, how uncertain it was and why it was shown or withheld.
Every release has sign-off from model, data-rights, privacy/compliance, security, reliability and product owners.

model_owned_projection_pipeline.design_principle: The model owns the projection; sources own observations; the contest engine owns constraints; the evidence layer owns explanation; the registry owns promotion. Do not let a source, heuristic rank, LLM narrative or optimizer silently become the projection.

pipeline_steps.name: Decision spine and identity
pipeline_steps.input: sport, league, game/event, contest/slate, player/team/official/venue identities
pipeline_steps.output: resolved canonical entities and effective-dated relationships
pipeline_steps.required_contract: provider-neutral sport-scoped IDs, alias history, source IDs, resolution confidence, unresolved/quarantine status
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: block projection if the entity or contest context is not resolved; never merge by name alone

pipeline_steps.name: Immutable observation ledger
pipeline_steps.input: raw provider responses, official reports, odds/lines, salaries, news, weather, tracking and user/league inputs where consented
pipeline_steps.required_contract: source_id, fetched_at, source_as_of, available_at/created_at, content_hash, parser_version, rights_snapshot, correction/void lineage
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: quarantine missing timestamps, rights, hashes or parser version; expose stale/conflict state

pipeline_steps.name: Point-in-time feature materialization
pipeline_steps.input: observations and feature definitions at a decision timestamp t0
pipeline_steps.output: FeatureSnapshot keyed by entity, slate/game, t0, feature-set version and rights state
pipeline_steps.required_contract: event_time <= t0 and available_at/created_at <= t0; explicit missingness; no live reads during training
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: return missing/stale/blocked feature state; do not backfill future knowledge or silently use latest values

pipeline_steps.name: Role and availability state model
pipeline_steps.input: injury/availability reports, depth charts, transactions, lineups, rotations, historical role and coach/team context
pipeline_steps.output: availability probability, expected minutes/snaps/plate appearances, role distribution and scenario states
pipeline_steps.required_contract: observed vs inferred status, report timestamp, confidence, replacement graph, minutes/role uncertainty
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: widen player distribution, propagate replacement effects and/or abstain when status is stale or contradictory

pipeline_steps.name: Sport-specific hierarchical distribution model
pipeline_steps.input: PIT FeatureSnapshot plus role state, market priors and historical labels
pipeline_steps.output: joint player/team/game distributions and conditional scenario forecasts
pipeline_steps.required_contract: model artifact ID, feature schema hash, training snapshot ID, label schema, sport/league/season scope, latent covariance and aggregation constraints
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: fallback only to a versioned baseline; otherwise abstain. Never substitute manual constants or LLM prose for a model output

pipeline_steps.name: Calibration and uncertainty wrapper
pipeline_steps.input: raw probabilities/distributions and held-out calibration residuals
pipeline_steps.output: calibrated probabilities, quantiles/intervals, coverage estimate, sharpness and refusal state
pipeline_steps.required_contract: calibration version, fit window, segment, target coverage, empirical coverage, interval width, sample count and drift state
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: withhold or widen interval when coverage, sample size or drift fails; do not label an interval guaranteed beyond its method/assumptions

pipeline_steps.name: Ownership and contest decision layer
pipeline_steps.input: calibrated player distributions, ownership distribution, salaries, contest rules, field size, payout curve and user constraints
pipeline_steps.output: expected fantasy points, percentile outcomes, leverage, duplication-adjusted utility, lineup set and risk metrics
pipeline_steps.required_contract: ProjectionRun ID, ContestSlate ID, scoring-rule version, optimizer seed, ownership model ID, simulation count and constraint hash
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: no lineup if salary/eligibility/late-swap/identity data is stale or incomplete; show missing-data state

pipeline_steps.name: Evaluation and promotion
pipeline_steps.input: sealed historical replay, live shadow predictions, realized labels/settlements and baseline predictions
pipeline_steps.required_contract: temporal splits, leakage report, proper scores, calibration, coverage, ranking/utility, CLV where relevant, subgroup slices, confidence intervals and kill-line result
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: stay shadow or blocked; never promote because a single slate or hit-rate slice looks good

pipeline_steps.name: Serving and evidence publication
pipeline_steps.output: customer payload with projection, uncertainty, freshness, factors, source lineage, counter-evidence, limitations and gate state
pipeline_steps.required_contract: public probability separated from internal score/edge/rank; exact model/data versions and timestamps; explanation generated from persisted contributions
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: blocked-stale, blocked-insufficient-evidence, blocked-rights, blocked-calibration or review state; never fabricate a reason

pipeline_steps.name: Monitoring, feedback and retraining
pipeline_steps.input: source health, feature/prediction drift, user feedback, delayed labels, settlement outcomes, optimizer results and incident logs
pipeline_steps.output: alerts, recalibration/retraining proposals, model rollback/kill decisions and a controlled feedback dataset
pipeline_steps.required_contract: model/data version dimensions, denominator definitions, delayed-label handling, bot/duplicate suppression, privacy/consent scope and owner
pipeline_steps.failure_behavior: pause affected sport/market or revert to champion/baseline; do not let feedback directly change weights without a versioned training decision

minimum_durable_schema.purpose: provider-neutral sport-scoped identity and effective-dated alias/crosswalk state
immutable raw input with timing, rights, parser and hash provenance
versioned, point-in-time materialized inputs and missingness state
outcome/settlement semantics, score rules and revisions
immutable model package, registry metadata, approval and rollback lineage
model-owned point and distribution forecasts for a decision timestamp
selection probability and uncertainty kept separate from performance probability
reproducible contest decision with seed, constraints, simulation and model versions

what_not_to_do: Do not train on latest tables without as-of/created-at filtering.
Do not call manual illustrative constants model-owned projections.
Do not blend probability, edge, rank, confidence, ownership and narrative into one unexplained number.
Do not activate a source because it is publicly visible; rights and redistribution are separate gates.
Do not treat tests, fixtures, or a backtest harness as historical proof until sealed point-in-time replay and evaluation receipts exist.
Do not use sensitive health/wearable/cognitive data without consent, minimization, purpose limitation and access controls.

expanded_research_conclusion.bottom_line: The next bottleneck is not finding another hundred feeds. It is converting the existing breadth into a trustworthy temporal data contract, durable fantasy schema, model registry, distributional/ownership model, and sealed evaluation loop. The second pass found that the repository is stronger in gates, evidence vocabulary and deterministic testing than its durable fantasy/model artifacts suggest, and weaker in point-in-time semantics, model ownership, contest-state persistence, operational SLO/privacy/security evidence and production drift controls than its documentation breadth suggests.
